findings.title: Actual intake receipts are not tied to the frozen original identity or multipart coordinates
findings.reasoning: The intake predicate compares response namespace/externalId only with its submitted body. It never compares either coordinate with frozen.identity or the actual importer's ordered part naming. A genuine successful intake of the exact frozen bytes under another namespace or externalId therefore satisfies this predicate. For multipart, unrelated/relabelled part-record identities can be put in the ordered request as long as each receipt agrees with itself. Matching provider, sourceRevision, byte digest and normalized record does not establish the original Source identity. mediaType, coverage and rights evidence are also not compared to the actual elected importer envelope; an arbitrary rightsEvidence object is enough.
required_assertions: Start with successful, contract-valid single-part and multipart intake request/response pairs and the exact frozen record. Assert original provider/kind/externalId for single parts and the importer's kind-dataset-part / externalId:part:index coordinates for every ordered multipart part. Do not require a multipart part-record to equal the canonical original Source record.

Change namespace or externalId consistently in both a genuine-shaped intake body and its successful matching observation, leaving bytes and the retained frozen identity unchanged: readiness must refuse for the coordinate mismatch rather than missing receipt. Exercise each of the four retainedAdmissionCases.

Bind the real importer mediaType, retention, coverage and source rights evidence to the frozen record/part and acknowledged observation. Do not infer authority or rights from a string UUID or a self-consistent unrelated request.
findings.owner: existing audit producer and dataset importer/Source intake owners
findings.disposition: Open; repair before treating import validation as complete. No intake was executed for this review.

findings.title: The actual importer record envelope is reduced to record and loses frozen snapshot/edge/image checks
findings.reasoning: For format rezics-dataset-record-v1, validation compares payload.record alone. The real importer serializes snapshot, digest, record, outgoing edges and images. An actually acknowledged envelope with the correct complete normalized DatasetRecord but a wrong snapshot id/digest, omitted or changed outgoing edges, or wrong images passes this comparison. retainedRequest.snapshot may still equal the frozen pin and retainedRequest.payload may accurately digest these wrong bytes: neither check joins the envelope metadata back to that pin/selection. This is distinct from the intentionally different normalized-record and raw/assembled-byte digests.
required_assertions: Exercise actual importer-shaped record envelopes for both single-part and multipart paths. Compare snapshot/digest and exact elected original-index outgoing-edge/image content to frozen normalized inputs, without rewriting their selection, original indexes or digests.

Construct a positive acknowledged envelope, then change each envelope metadata field while preserving the exact record; generate matching successful intake receipts and matching actual assembled byte metadata so validation reaches the envelope comparison. Assert the specific mismatch refusal.

Keep valid provider-data/Bangumi api_subject representations only where the existing consumer actually accepts them. Do not substitute a hand-invented minimal envelope for the real importer representation.
findings.coverage_gap: The unit mutation at lines 355-357 replaces part bytes without replacing the recorded intake request/response. It is rejected at import-intake-receipts before payload validation. A generic toThrow cannot prove the envelope guard. The positive fixture uses provider data/api_subject, with an enlarged synthetic MusicBrainz artist for multipart; it does not exercise an actual importer record envelope.

findings.title: Observed synopsis support can be stale, withdrawn or tied to different field heads while satisfying the guard
findings.reasoning: The optional synopsisSupport branch correctly demands a matching control URL/support id and private management id/source/target/conversion. It does not join the expectedWorkHead, field/content/control basis, source mapping, mapped value, actingSubject or full terminal control result to the target, nor management state/slot/mappingRevision/valueDigest/nativeRevision/graphReceipt/headGuarantee/outcome to that result. A genuine old successful source-control receipt (including replay), together with a current management receipt now marked withdrawn for the same support/source/conversion, still satisfies every predicate. The existing private support schema explicitly carries those distinguishing fields. The positive unit bypasses the real request contract: it omits required expectedWorkHead, basis, value, source.mapping and actingSubject and fabricates a response containing only support; its private response omits the management fields. That passing shape does not demonstrate an executable existing-owner prerequisite.
required_assertions: Keep synopsisSupport absent when unobserved. When present, start from a contract-valid actual command/result and the existing private management response, joining the exact target/slot, pre-command work and field basis, resulting content/control heads, original source record/observation/conversion, mapping and support receipt coordinates.

Refuse a withdrawn or wrong-slot support, stale/mismatched work/native/control/content head, wrong mapping/normalization/value digest or receipt guarantee, unrelated caller and reused support result from a different target. Use an otherwise valid prerequisite and assert the specific failed join.

Preserve the independent same-value human confirmation and withdrawal/replay assertions in import-outcomes. Do not move proposed Source admission success into setup or fabricate new server interface results.

predecessor_findings.title: Fresh import staging loses the journals that bind original source records to native Works
predecessor_findings.concrete_source_case: On a fresh isolated restore containing the 113 original Works, import a frozen Work record already represented in originals. The producer copies snapshot.json and blobs into a new run-local inputRoot, but supplies neither the original import journals nor an admitted native binding interface. importDataset can reuse identities only from that inputRoot/imports and matching mainOrigin/actingSubject/dataEpoch. The new root has no such journal; the fresh localhost endpoint also participates in replay-key identityContext. The record therefore enters freshWorks with expectedWorkHead:null and no input.work; the service derives Work/Main/revisions from a new admission. verifyOriginals merely rereads the old bindings, so retaining the old Work alongside a duplicate does not fail that check.
predecessor_findings.impact: Original IDs may remain present while projections/relationships adopt newly created duplicates. Existence checks do not establish replay onto the same original 113 source-to-native identities or preserved original edge/role correspondence.
required_assertions: For every imported original source identity, the importer result/journal resolves to the retained resource, Main, revision and applicable occurrence/role bindings; no second Work is admitted.

Replay after a restored endpoint change uses the existing owner-supported journal/receipt identity mechanism and preserves uncertain-request custody. Count and identity assertions detect duplication, not merely survival of old reads.
predecessor_findings.disposition: Producer repair needs an existing importer/journal owner decision for safe retained-binding reuse across isolated origins. Do not manufacture a journal, overwrite historical requests, map by title, inject business state or assign replacement IDs.

predecessor_findings.title: Nonterminal and rejected publication responses can complete a successful stage
predecessor_findings.concrete_source_case: A recipe command POST /v1/content-publications can set expected status 202. The real route returns 202 for result.status=pending. A rejected publication returns 200 and can likewise match expected status 200. assertAuditRecipe accepts both; AuditRecorder.command checks only the numeric match, publishes receipt/command bindings and allows stage-completed. There is no required terminal publication-body assertion. A recipe whose generic readiness probes concern other records can continue without proving this publication succeeded.
predecessor_findings.impact: The recorded HTTP answer is genuine, but it is promoted into the producer successful-stage namespace while publication is pending or rejected. Dependent references and a ready source are not tied to exact terminal publication/eligibility receipts.

predecessor_findings.title: Flat string provenance does not bind typed identity, revision or generation coordinates
predecessor_findings.concrete_source_case: AuditRecorder.bind collects every string recursively. command:<id> includes the submitted request body, caller, path and response, so a literal native IRI supplied as prose/evidence enters observed even if no owner result created or identified that resource. predecessor_findings.title: Host-admission accounting corrupts phase timing and still consumes the absolute deadline
predecessor_findings.concrete_source_case: restoreCatalogueBackup returns raw startupMs containing admission and also admissionWaitMs separately. liveAuditRuntime.open subtracts admission from totalMs, then computes readinessMs=activeTotal-rawRestore-rawStartup. For raw restore 1000 ms, raw startup 110000 ms containing 100000 ms admission, and post-start/readiness/persona work 5000 ms, active total is 16000 ms but emitted readinessMs is -95000 ms. The imports consumer rejects negative values. Independently, AbortSignal.timeout(budget.remaining()) is created before host admission; excluding admission after restore cannot extend that already-running wall-clock signal.
